title: Handle XF86_RFKILL keysym to provide keyboard shortcut for toggling airplane mode
line: The laptop airplane mode key (and the Wi-Fi key) now toggles airplane mode, with an OSD, and the shortcut can be changed in System Settings > Shortcuts > Networking.
explanation: Airplane mode only existed as a switch in the Networks widget: no global shortcut called it, and the XF86RFKill keysym that laptops send for their airplane key has no Qt key at all, so KWin turned it into key 0 and no shortcut could ever match it. KWin now maps XF86RFKill to Qt::Key_WLAN (like it already aliases other keysyms), and plasma-nm's kded module registers a "Toggle Airplane Mode" global shortcut (component "Networking", default the Wi-Fi key) that runs the same Handler::enableAirplaneMode code as the widget, updates the shared setting so the widget follows, and shows an "Airplane Mode On/Off" OSD. Because the shortcut and the widget use separate Handler instances, Handler now turns Wi-Fi, WWAN and Bluetooth back on when it is asked to leave airplane mode that it didn't enable itself, instead of leaving them off.

commits.message:
xkb: treat the XF86RFKill key like the WLAN key

Qt has no key for XF86RFKill, which many laptops send for their airplane
mode key, so that key could never trigger a global shortcut. Map it to
Qt::Key_WLAN, so it does whatever the Wi-Fi key is set to do.

BUG: 349744

kded: add a global shortcut to toggle airplane mode

Airplane mode could only be toggled from the Networks widget. Add a
global shortcut for it, on the Wi-Fi/airplane key by default, with an
OSD, and turn the radios back on even if it was enabled elsewhere.

BUG: 349744

patches.diff:
From 17319aec1821285603b1dfe6f3904199f1f39721 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 12:26:59 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] xkb: treat the XF86RFKill key like the WLAN key

Qt has no key for XF86RFKill, which many laptops send for their airplane
mode key, so that key could never trigger a global shortcut. Map it to
Qt::Key_WLAN, so it does whatever the Wi-Fi key is set to do.

BUG: 349744
---
 src/xkb.cpp | 3 +++
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)

diff --git a/src/xkb.cpp b/src/xkb.cpp
index f5c6225a83..3346a46f33 100644
--- a/src/xkb.cpp
+++ b/src/xkb.cpp
@@ -969,6 +969,9 @@ Qt::Key Xkb::toQtKey(xkb_keysym_t keySym,
     if (qtKey > 0xff && keySym <= 0xff) {
         // XKB_KEY_mu, XKB_KEY_ydiaeresis go here
         qtKey = Qt::Key(keySym);
+    } else if (keySym == XKB_KEY_XF86RFKill) {
+        // Qt has no key for it, treat it like the WLAN key so it can toggle airplane mode
+        qtKey = Qt::Key_WLAN;
     }
     return qtKey;
 }
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Master: pressing XF86RFKill (and XF86WLAN) with the Networks widget open does nothing; Wi-Fi and Bluetooth stay on.
Patched: pressing XF86RFKill turns airplane mode on, shows the OSD, the widget's airplane switch follows and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth go off.
Master: searching "airplane" in System Settings > Shortcuts finds nothing.
Patched: Networking > Toggle Airplane Mode, default shortcut Wireless (the Wi-Fi/airplane key), can be changed or extended.
